description: A composite figure pairing a numeric data table with a back-scattered-electron (BSE) SEM micrograph, both concerning 600 °C tempered Fe-Mn-Al-C lightweight steel. The left panel is Table 3, "EDS for Al and Mn in 9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C", giving wt% values with Min/Mean/Max rows for four constituents (δ, γ, K, γ nano-k). Al varies narrowly (δ 7.8-8.7, γ 7.6-8.0, K 8.0-8.3, γ nano-k 7.8-8.1 wt%), while Mn is higher and more scattered (δ 9.7-10.0, γ 9.9-10.7, k 10.2-10.5, and γ nano-k distinctly highest at 13.2-13.6 wt%). The right panel is a BSE-SEM micrograph (100 µm scale bar) showing a strongly banded, lath-like structure: light, elongated parallel bands labelled "γ+κ lamellae" alternating with darker matrix regions labelled "γα+coarse κ". The figure is captioned as precipitation transformation in 600 °C tempered 12Al-10Mn-1C, so the caption's alloy name and the table's title alloy (9Al-10Mn-1C) disagree. Together the panels argue that tempering at 600 °C yields a banded γ+κ lamellar structure coexisting with coarse κ, with the nano-κ constituent being the Mn-richest phase.

observations.observation: Table 3 reports EDS Al and Mn contents in wt% for the constituents δ, γ, K and γ nano-k of a 600 °C tempered alloy, listed as Min, Mean and Max.
Al content is similar across all four constituents, with mean values between 7.8 and 8.2 wt% (ranges: δ 7.8-8.7, γ 7.6-8.0, K 8.0-8.3, γ nano-k 7.8-8.1 wt%).
Mn content in the γ nano-k constituent is clearly the highest, ranging from 13.2 to 13.6 wt% (mean 13.4), compared with δ (9.7-10.0), γ (9.9-10.7) and k (10.2-10.5) wt%.
The SEM micrograph carries a 100 µm scale bar.
Two features are explicitly labelled in the micrograph: 'γ+κ lamellae' (light elongated bands) and 'γα+coarse κ' (darker matrix regions).
The microstructure is strongly banded, with light lath-like bands roughly parallel and alternating with darker bands.
The figure caption names the alloy as 12Al-10Mn-1C, whereas the table title names 9Al-10Mn-1C; the two sample identities within this figure group disagree.
The caption describes the figure as precipitation transformation in 600 °C tempered alloys, implying the micrograph shows the transformation products after tempering.

The citing text describes the 600 °C transformation in 12Al-10Mn-1C as a 'more complex random-like transformation', not as ordered discontinuous precipitation, and labels it a 'generic precipitation transformation'.
The citing text states that both γ+κ lamellae and alternated bands of two apparently different austenite grades are observable in this figure.
